headline: Fruita Campground and Scenic Drive Access Checks
reservation: Individual campsites at Fruita must be reserved months in advance through recreation.gov; there are no first-come, first-served sites in the main valley. Backcountry permits are required for overnight trekking and must be obtained at the visitor center; verify current road access for the Scenic Drive before arrival.

days.title: Fruita History and Petroglyphs

stops.name: Fruita Historic District
stops.detail: Explore the pioneer orchards and Gifford House while learning about the Fremont River valley history.

stops.name: Capitol Reef Petroglyphs
stops.detail: View ancient rock art from the designated boardwalks along Utah State Route 24.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; conditions vary based on SR-24 traffic
days.note: Orchard picking is seasonal; check the U-Pick signs for daily availability and rules.

days.title: Natural Bridges and Viewpoints
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Hickman Bridge
stops.detail: Hike the moderate two-mile trail to a 133-foot natural bridge with views of the Waterpocket Fold.

stops.name: Panorama Point
stops.detail: Observe the expansive red rock landscape and the 'Goosenecks' of Sulphur Creek.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; rocky terrain near trailheads requires careful driving
days.note: Hickman Bridge trail has switchbacks and uneven rock; wear sturdy footwear.

days.title: Canyons and Domes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Scenic Drive

stops.name: Grand Wash
stops.detail: Walk through narrow canyon walls to see the unique geology of the Waterpocket Fold.

stops.name: Capitol Dome
stops.detail: View the Navajo Sandstone formation that resembles the U.S. Capitol building.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; the Scenic Drive has narrow sections and gravel spurs
days.note: Avoid Grand Wash if there is any forecast of rain due to extreme flash flood risk.

intel.title: Hickman Bridge Lot
intel.text: The trailhead lot for Hickman Bridge is small and typically fills by mid-morning during peak spring months. Consider arriving early or visiting late in the afternoon to secure a space.

intel.title: Desert Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent throughout most of the park's interior and canyon trails. Download offline maps and park brochures in Torrey before entering the park boundaries.

intel.title: Gateway Fuel Stations
intel.text: Torrey is the last reliable location for fuel and water before entering the park's central corridor. There are no services, including fuel or groceries, inside Capitol Reef National Park.

intel.title: Flash Flood Alerts
intel.text: Monsoon season in late summer can cause sudden, dangerous flooding in washes and narrow canyons. Always check the daily weather forecast at the visitor center before entering Grand Wash.

intel.title: Unpaved Road Hazards
intel.text: Cathedral Valley and Burr Trail roads are unpaved and can become impassable for all vehicles after rain. Check the official NPS road conditions page before attempting any travel off the paved highway.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at CNY and drive approximately three hours to Torrey. Visit the park visitor center for current maps and weather alerts before checking into your hotel.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD is recommended for remote districts like Cathedral Valley; standard cars are fine for SR-24. Check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved roads.
plan.goldenHour: Panorama Point offers sunset views over the Henry Mountains and the park's red rock domes.
